review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib for existing metric-median or metric-betweenness definitions. I found none: the only betweenness notion is `Wbtw` in the affine/convex files, which is an affine-ray notion and not the metric `dist a b = dist a m + dist m b` condition. I treated the lemmas that overlap Mathlib results, such as `exists_unitBall_dual_maximizer` and `segment_point_distances`, as theorem-level overlap, which the rubric excludes. The `SignedUnitRepresentation`, `aggregateSet` and `HasEndpointScaling` structures are problem-specific, and I found no Mathlib counterpart. The one reportable item is the in-file duplicate `IsMetricMedian`, which is weak. I only grepped for uses of `IsMetricMedian` and did not read the other Mahler files in full.

findings.excerpt:
def IsMetricMedian (x : Fin 3 → E) (m : E) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, i ≠ j → dist (x i) (x j) = dist (x i) m + dist m (x j)
findings.problem: The file defines the metric-median predicate twice. `IsMetricMedian x m` is stated for a normed space `E`. `HasMetricMedians` then restates the identical body inline instead of using it, and its binder is only `PseudoMetricSpace`. `IsMetricMedian` is never used anywhere in the repository; the grep for it finds only its own definition. It is therefore a dead, competing version of the concept that `HasMetricMedians` already spells out. The lemmas such as `metricMedians_of_zero_medians` and `dist_extreme_unit_eq_two` also repeat the unfolded form (`dist (x i) (x j) = dist (x i) m + dist m (x j)`) instead of naming it.
findings.proposed_change: Make `IsMetricMedian` the single notion, generalised to `[PseudoMetricSpace E]`, and define `HasMetricMedians E := ∀ x : Fin 3 → E, ∃ m, IsMetricMedian x m`. Alternatively, delete the unused `IsMetricMedian`. If it is kept, use it in the statements and proofs (`hm i j hij`) so there is one named predicate.
findings.benefit: This removes a redundant unused definition and leaves one canonical, reusable name for the median condition. It also means the three-point condition no longer has to be re-derived in proofs.
